title: Gemini 4 Carbon early test results are in ahead of release
content:
Gemini 4 Argon has only been public for about a week, and Google already seems to be lining up its successor. Gemini 4 Carbon, the checkpoint Business Insider first reported on inside Google's Jetski coding tool earlier this month, now appears to be reaching people outside the company.
According to X user Lentils, a Carbon early access program has started, with partners getting access and the model being tested on LM Arena. They expect a release "very close" and describe Carbon as noticeably better than Argon at 3D work, while frontend and UI output is still weak. It's also slower, though, in their words, "less lazy."
Meanwhile, reliable leaker Lyra also quoted that post with a screenshot of Google's Gemini API Early Access Program docs, which describe an invite-only group of developers, researchers and partners getting upcoming Gemini API and AI Studio models before launch.
The Trusted Tester Agreement is quite clear: unreleased models, codenames, benchmarks, and outputs should remain private until launch, and the models shouldn’t be used in production. Google asks testers to send evaluations and comparisons privately, making the steady stream of Carbon outputs on X awkward.
Now, on the early outputs, Lumina shared most of them in multiple posts. They say Carbon has been on Arena since yesterday and that it's a clear improvement over Argon. However, they noted it's "incredibly slow," roughly two to four times slower depending on the task. Their voxel pagoda comparison sets Carbon next to other frontier models, and they say it has "noticeably higher quality than Argon does."
They also ran the classic SVG pelican on a bicycle test. Again, they call out weak UI and slow speed, but say Carbon otherwise "feels good" across the wide range of tasks they've tried.
It's worth noting, however, that these are arena matchups and hand-picked prompts, not benchmarks, and nobody can be sure which checkpoint they're served.
While we wait for the new Carbon model to arrive, Logan Kilpatrick also just posted that Google processed around 25 trillion tokens in the first 72 hours after Argon launched. So Google might want to keep up its pace before the hype dies down.
A faster cadence of Gemini 4 checkpoints would also matter beyond the chatbot. We recently spotted broader Computer Use permissions in the Gemini desktop app, and Google appears to be building Nano Banana 3 Pro on top of Gemini 4, with a November to December window in view.
Meanwhile, Google isn't the only company pushing new models left and right. OpenAI is preparing GPT-6.1 Terra, which has surfaced in Microsoft code, and Anthropic's Fable 5.5 is already reaching partners, with several more models apparently on the way. If Carbon fixes Argon's 3D weaknesses without making users wait too long, Google could have a strong answer ready.
We'll have to wait and test it ourselves once it arrives before jumping to conclusions.

report.summary: Early testers say Google's Gemini 4 Carbon beats Argon at 3D work but is slower and weak on frontend/UI, with a launch expected soon.
report.background: Gemini 4 Argon has been public for only about a week, yet Google appears to be preparing its successor, Gemini 4 Carbon. Business Insider first reported the Carbon checkpoint inside Google's internal Jetski coding tool. Carbon now appears to be reaching external partners through an invite-only early access program and is being tested on LM Arena. The timing reflects intense model competition: OpenAI is preparing GPT-6.1 Terra, Anthropic's Fable 5.5 is reaching partners, and Google processed roughly 25 trillion tokens in Argon's first 72 hours. Google is also reportedly building Nano Banana 3 Pro on Gemini 4 and expanding Computer Use permissions, making a faster checkpoint cadence important beyond the chatbot.
key_points: Carbon is reaching outside Google through an invite-only early access program for developers, researchers, and partners. Testers reportedly have access to upcoming Gemini API and AI Studio models, and Carbon has appeared on LM Arena. Google's Trusted Tester Agreement says unreleased models, codenames, benchmarks, and outputs should stay private until launch, making public Carbon posts awkward.

Early impressions say Carbon is noticeably better than Argon at 3D work and has higher voxel-output quality, but frontend and UI output remains weak. Testers also describe Carbon as 'incredibly slow,' roughly two to four times slower depending on the task, though one called it 'less lazy.' These are arena matchups and hand-picked prompts, not formal benchmarks.

There is uncertainty about exactly which Carbon checkpoint testers are using. The reports come from X users sharing screenshots and generated outputs, not controlled evaluations. That makes it hard to judge whether observed strengths and weaknesses will hold in the final release, especially for coding, UI, and latency-sensitive applications.

Google may be trying to sustain momentum after Argon's rapid adoption. Argon drew about 25 trillion processed tokens in 72 hours, but rivals are also moving fast: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra has surfaced in Microsoft code, and Anthropic's Fable 5.5 is reaching partners. If Carbon fixes Argon's 3D weaknesses without excessive slowness, Google could have a strong competitive answer.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Carbon signals that frontier-model releases are becoming faster, more iterative checkpoint drops rather than annual events. For developers, early access could shorten the gap between model launch and production integration, but the Trusted Tester Agreement's no-production rule and unclear checkpoint identities mean teams should wait for official API documentation and benchmarks. For regular users, Carbon may bring better 3D and spatial outputs, yet weak UI generation and 2-4x slower responses could hurt interactive products. The bigger lesson is that leaks and arena hype are not substitutes for controlled evaluation; latency, reliability, and frontend quality will decide whether Carbon is a meaningful upgrade or just another fast-following checkpoint.
report.tools: Watch LM Arena for side-by-side comparisons, Google AI Studio and the Gemini API Early Access Program for official access, and Google's Gemini API docs for launch details. Developers can use LM Arena prompts to track 3D, UI, and latency differences, but should validate against their own benchmarks before production use.
